name: The Pine of the Arsène Crossroads

location.address: Route forestière, parcelle 98, Forêt domaniale de Roumare, near Montigny/Canteleu

access: Free, public ONF-managed forest, no restrictions. Waymarked as part of the official 'arbres remarquables' trail (interpretive panel on site).
transport: No public transport reaches the forest. By car: from Montigny take the D86 towards Deville-les-Rouen, park about 750m along at the first forest-road junction (near the barrier, not in front of it), then walk about 150m on the closed forest road between parcelles 96 and 90 to the crossroads.
verify_notes: Solitary Scots pine standing out among broadleaf trees at a named forest crossroads (carrefour Arsene). One of 13 trees/groups jointly designated 'remarkable' since 2019 by Metropole Rouen Normandie, the ONF and the national A.R.B.R.E.S. association (partnership since 2002). Register gives exact GPS (49 27' 42.407" N / 1 1' 11.117" E, matches sigapp coordinates closely) plus turn-by-turn walking directions from the parking spot, so pin is tree-level. Diameter given as 'diametre au pied' (measured at the base/foot of the trunk, not the usual 1.3m breast height), 75cm; girth_cm above is pi x diameter (236cm) and is NOT directly comparable to breast-height girths recorded elsewhere on the site because of the different measurement point. Age band as given by the register (110/120 years); no update-since date is stated on the panel so treat the band as roughly current. Register text: 'Ce resineux marque le carrefour, il emerge d'un accompagnement proche d'arbres feuillus. Il est et restera un temoin du peuplement forestier de pins encore presents' (it marks the crossroads, a witness to the pine stands still present in the forest). No news of storm damage found for this specific tree.

name: The Gadeau de Kerville Oak

location.address: Carrefour du Petit Charme, parcelle 206, Foret domaniale de Roumare, near Quevillon
location.neighbourhood: Foret de Roumare, near the Parc animalier / arboretum du Petit Charme, Quevillon

access: Free, public ONF-managed forest, no restrictions. Waymarked as part of the official 'arbres remarquables' trail (interpretive panel on site).
transport: No public transport reaches the forest. By car: park at either the Parc animalier car parks or the arboretum du Petit Charme car park; the oak stands on the path circling the mare Epinay, at the start of the single forest road, at the carrefour du Petit Charme.
verify_notes: IMPORTANT NAMING CAVEAT, checked against a genuinely independent source (French Wikipedia's Foret de Roumare article, sourced footnote): 'La foret a souffert de la tempete de decembre 1999; le chene Gadeau de Kerville, plusieurs fois centenaire, a ete deracine a l'occasion de cet accident meteorologique' -- the ORIGINAL oak carrying this name, described elsewhere as roughly 280 years old and named in 1937, was uprooted in the December 1999 storm. The tree now registered under this name (104cm base diameter, 26m tall, register's own age estimate 120/150 years, meaning planted circa 1875-1905) is necessarily a DIFFERENT, younger oak at or near the same crossroads that has inherited the commemorative name since being added to the register (a Cirkwi listing places this current designation from 2019). DO NOT write this as if it is the tree Henri Gadeau de Kerville himself catalogued in his 1890s survey 'Les vieux arbres de la Normandie' -- that was the tree lost in 1999. The honest story is: a successor oak near the same spot carries forward the name of Rouen's own 19th-century naturalist, who pioneered the 'arbre remarquable' concept in Normandy (113 trees catalogued 1890-1932, published via the Bulletin de la Societe des Amis des Sciences naturelles de Rouen, originals held at Gallica/BnF). Diameter given as 'diametre au pied' (base, not breast height); girth_cm above is pi x diameter (327cm).

verify_notes: One collectible point: a beech and a sessile oak growing directly beside each other despite very different light and longevity requirements, on the path around the Mare Epinay. Register's own text: 'Il est rare de trouver assembles deux sujets de grande taille et d'essence n'ayant pas les memes exigences de lumiere, ni la meme longevite, aussi proche l'un de l'autre' (it is rare to find two large trees of species with such different light needs and lifespans standing this close together). Flagged because the register gives a single diameter/height/age figure (90cm / 30m / 90-120 years) for the PAIR rather than one value per species; it is not stated whether this is an average, a shared figure, or describes only one of the two individuals -- the writer should describe both trees as a pair rather than quote one measurement as belonging to a specific one of them. Diameter is 'diametre au pied' (base, not breast height); girth_cm above is pi x the given diameter (283cm).

Diameter is 'diametre au pied' (base, not breast height); girth_cm above uses the midpoint of the given range (56cm) x pi (176cm), so treat as a rough figure covering two trees of somewhat different size rather than one precise measurement.

name: The Five Brothers

location.address: Parcelle 73, off the D121 between Mont-Saint-Aignan and Houppeville, Foret domaniale Verte

access: Free, public ONF-managed forest, no restrictions. Waymarked as part of the official 'arbres remarquables' trail.
transport: No public transport reaches the forest. By car: from the D121 (between Mont-Saint-Aignan and Houppeville) park at the parcelle 69 car park (former V1 site); at the back of the car park take the path on the right at the start of the Grand Canton forest road, and where it bends 90 degrees continue straight on the footpath. The 'bouquet' stands not far inside parcelle 73, among broadleaf trees.
verify_notes: Register calls it a 'bouquet d'arbres' (a bouquet/cluster of trees) of Abies grandis at one pinned location, which is why it is treated as one collectible ensemble rather than scattered individuals; the name 'les cinq freres' (the five brothers) implies five closely grown stems, though the register's own text does not spell out the count or whether the trunks are fused or simply five trees grown close together, and no on-site photo was viewed to confirm the exact form. Flagged for that reason; a future photo pass should confirm the arrangement before writing a confident physical description. Notably YOUNG for this project at only about 50 years (register gives a single flat figure, not a range, so a small +-5 year band is applied here rather than treating it as precise), but reaching 39m tall and a 110cm base diameter in that time on this North American conifer is itself the remarkable fact -- unusually fast growth rather than age is the story. Girth_cm above is pi x the given base diameter (346cm); note this is a base measurement, not breast height.

name: The Calabrian Pine of the Jardin des Plantes

location.address: Jardin des Plantes de Rouen, 7 rue de Trianon, 76100 Rouen
location.neighbourhood: Jardin des Plantes, Rive Gauche, Rouen

access: Free, open daily; municipal botanical garden.
transport: Inside Rouen itself, reachable on foot or by tram/bus from the city centre (Jardin des Plantes tram stop on line T2/T3 is a short walk away); no forest drive needed, unlike the rest of this batch.
verify_notes: The ONE tree in this batch actually inside Rouen rather than in the outlying forests, worth the page for that alone (per the six-things brief: 'a city page whose every entry is a forest drive is a worse afternoon than one with two trees you can walk to from the station'). Source is the City of Rouen's own official press release (rouen.fr, 8 June 2021, fetched via Wayback Machine since the live page now 403s): a Pinus brutia ('Pin de Calabre') 'age de plus de 120 ans' (over 120 years old), described by the city as 'unique dans la region car il ne pousse habituellement pas sous nos latitudes. Originaire d'Asie mineure, il se rencontre aux abords de la mer noire' (unique in the region, not usually found this far north, native to Asia Minor near the Black Sea). The same article describes a 2021 rescue: the city installed a support structure ('etayage') because the tree was at risk of collapsing. FLAGGED for two reasons: (1) only one source found, the municipal press release itself; no independent second source (press, botanical literature, A.R.B.R.E.S.) turned up in this pass corroborating the age or the species identification, so a second pass should try French-language botanical/heritage sources or the garden's own on-site labels. (2) location_precision is approximate: only the garden's own general coordinates are known (an 8-hectare garden), not the tree's exact position within it; no plan or photo located this pass pinpointing which bed or path it stands on. No girth/diameter figure was given by the source, so girth_cm is left empty rather than estimated.

name: The Beeches of Roche Fouet

location.address: On the waymarked 'Les Troglodytes' circuit, within the ruins of the Roche Fouet castle site, parcelle 458, Foret domaniale de La Londe-Rouvray
location.neighbourhood: Foret de La Londe-Rouvray, near Orival / Les Essarts, overlooking the Seine

access: Free, public ONF-managed forest, no restrictions. Waymarked as part of both the official 'arbres remarquables' trail and the local 'Les Troglodytes' walking circuit through the Orival hillside.
transport: No public transport reaches the tree directly. By car: park at the entrance to the forest on the Les Essarts side (parcelle 150) and follow the waymarked 'Les Troglodytes' path; sturdy footwear needed, the path climbs and descends. Sits above the Seine near the Orival oppidum site.
verify_notes: Register's own text: 'Ces hetres, puisqu'il s'agit de plusieurs pieds, sont imbriques dans les ruines du chateau de la Roche Fouet dominant la Seine' (these beeches, several stems, are interwoven with the ruins of the Roche Fouet castle overlooking the Seine). The remarkable fact here is the SETTING (beech trunks growing through/among ruined castle stonework on a hillside above the Seine) rather than size or age: this is explicitly several stems ('plusieurs pieds'), youngest and smallest of the whole batch (only 40cm base diameter, 22m tall, register's own age estimate 40-60 years). Flagged because it is a multi-stem entry and the register gives one representative figure for the group, not one figure per stem, and because the historical detail of the castle ruins themselves (Roche Fouet / Orival oppidum) was not independently verified this pass beyond the register's own mention -- worth a follow-up check with a local-history or archaeology source before writing confidently about the ruins' age or origin. Furthest tree in this batch at about 14.5km from central Rouen, but on a genuine named, waymarked circuit. Diameter is 'diametre au pied' (base, not breast height); girth_cm above is pi x diameter (126cm).
